research_question: When did Google select elemental model codenames and public product labels, versus merely announcing them?

records.limits: No authenticated Google artifact, firsthand internal document or original reproducible model identifier in this audit; cannot establish exact internal selection date.

records.event: Google officially publicly announces Gemini 4 Argon
records.limits: Establishes public use, not originator or internal decision date.

records.event: Business Insider reports seeing Google internal documents/screenshots citing Argon, Barium, Carbon checkpoints; a document reportedly selected Barium-B as model released publicly under Argon brand
records.limits: Journalist sees alleged internal materials; readers cannot independently authenticate them. Barium-B checkpoint selection is distinct from selecting the word Argon. Google declined comment.

records.event: Google product leader Tulsee Doshi publicly discussed internal use of Argon and element naming
records.limits: Does not give original coiner/date or prove material access.

records.event: Carbon internal checkpoint documented in Business Insider reporting before public product announcement
records.limits: Does not authenticate exact naming-decision time or original selector.

records.event: Business Insider reports an internal message identifying Hydrogen as an internal name before its public launch
records.limits: Original internal message not provided as an independently inspectable artifact; exact earliest naming date remains unknown.
Earlier internal naming-decision evidence not authenticated in this pass.

precisions: A checkpoint identifier Barium-B and the public product label Argon are different variables and must not be collapsed.
Company product development lineage is not name-selection history.
Chronology precedence is not copying proof.
Published user-owned repo history does not itself prove Google staff accessed those repositories.
Original Argon punctuation is user's way of saying Argon; no further cellular mechanism audit intended.
